messages.subject: coord_flip confussion / feature request
parts:
I'm wondering what the rationale for having coord_flip() is. In my
view the use of it is mostly related to having box-and-whiskers,
violin, line range etc. plot flipped over.

I would think that the two former should just draw their orientation
from whether x or y are factor values and linerange should have an
x_linerange and y_linerange parallel. In my view this allows for far
more flexibility (especially in facetted plots), but is also more
intuitive...

e.g. given 'data' is our data.frame, class is a factor and value is
numeric:

p <- ggplot(data=data)

p + geom_boxplot(aes(x=factor, y=value))

could be flipped simply by:

p + geom_boxplot(aes(x=value, y=factor))

I don't think that coord_flip should necessary be abandoned but i
believe it is an unnecessary constraint that some geom orientation is
dependent on it...

Does this make sense for others

best wishes

Thomas

Eliminating the need for coord_flip() makes sense to me. It is something
I put on the wishlist
(https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/wishlist---feature-requests)
back when a few of us were brainstorming things we'd like to see.

I don't know if I would implement it as determining the direction based
on which dimensions are continuous and which are discrete. While this
would work for boxplot, it would not work for linerange/pointrange (as
you note). It would be problematic for density and histogram as well.

Hadley mentioned once the idea of a function which would take a geom and
return a flipped geom. I think that would be a good approach because
then there would not be effectively duplicated code in a geom that just
acted on different dimensions. That isn't something I'd want to try
until after the geom re-write from proto to S3.
